content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?The Situation Report's PostThe Situation Report1d · Shared with PublicApple names John Ternus as next CEO, succeeding Tim Cook on September 1.Here are some key facts about the transition:• Ternus, 50, is Apple's current SVP of Hardware Engineering and a company veteran since 2001• Apple has named John Ternus as its next chief executive officer, effective September 1, ending Tim Cook's 14-year run at the helm• Ternus, 50, is currently Apple's senior vice president of hardware engineering and has been with the company since 2001• He rose through the ranks from Apple's product design team, becoming a VP of hardware engineering in 2013 before joining the executive team in 2021• As hardware chief, Ternus oversaw some of Apple's most consequential product lines, including the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and AirPods• He played a key role in reigniting Mac sales, which have gained market share in recent years• Most recently, Ternus led the development of the iPhone Air, unveiled last fall and described as the biggest iPhone redesign since 2017• Cook, who succeeded co-founder Steve Jobs in 2011, will transition to executive chairman — the same role Jobs held before his death• Ternus is the same age Cook was when he first took over as CEO, and will also join Apple's board on September 1• The leadership change comes as Apple navigates growing AI-driven competition from rivals looking to loosen its grip on the consumer electronics market• Before Apple, Ternus worked as a mechanical engineer at Virtual Research Systems; he holds a degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Pennsylvania#TheSituationReportAll reactions:33 sharesLikeComment
